consumers: Rust codepet-core::agent (WP2: normalization, event ids, hmac_keys, interactivity, turn_qualifies, caps, sessions, fold, aggregate) and the generated petstate.js via test_state_machine.mjs / test_bar_model.mjs (WP6: priority) plus the WP5 popup (popup_routing, connect_card, helpers_rows); replayed by docs/v0.3/contracts/check_contracts.py

clients.name: Claude Code
clients.transport: shell command via Claude plugin hooks.json

clients.name: Hermes
clients.transport: argv spawn from the Hermes plugin

rules: argv client id is authoritative; the payload only passes a per-client schema sanity check
only top-level keys are read (depth 1); nested values are skipped unbuffered
id fields: strings <= 128 bytes of [A-Za-z0-9._:-], else the event is dropped (bad_id)
agent_id / subagentType present -> dropped before any write (child); this check runs first

codepet_test present -> the HOOK compares it (constant time) with $STATE/test.nonce (read with O_NOFOLLOW, regular file owned by the user, <= 64 bytes, trailing newline stripped). Equal -> the inbox record carries test:true. Missing nonce file, a different value, or a value that is not 32 lowercase hex -> the event is dropped (test_nonce) and never folded as a real event. Without codepet_test -> test:false. The fold never sees the nonce; it trusts the 0700 inbox
unmapped event names or notification types -> dropped (unmapped)

Grok: prefer hook_event_name (PascalCase); when only hookEventName (snake_case) is present it maps through grok_snake_event_names; camelCase ids (sessionId, promptId, toolUseId, notificationType, toolName)

synthesized payloads (OpenCode, Hermes; plugin-payload.schema.json): codepet_v must be the integer 1 and event one of the nine kinds, else unmapped. tools: an integer 0..=1000 (not a boolean), anything else is ignored (tools 0) and the event is kept. interactive: a boolean; anything else, or absent, is true. approval_key is read only for hermes, only with event waiting or activity and only without session_id (else bad_id / unmapped); OpenCode's approval_key is never read. completed/failed/interrupted are not on the allow-list: the Hermes plugin maps on_session_end itself and sends the kind
normalization.nonce_context: each vector's 'nonce' is the content of $STATE/test.nonce when the hook runs (absent key or null = no file)

grok-cli.Stop: reason end_turn -> turn_done; channel_closed/shutdown -> session_end; other -> dropped

opencode.(synthesized): event field is one of the nine kinds

hermes.(synthesized): event field is one of the nine kinds

event_ids.formula: dig = hex(sha256(bytes read))[..16]; event_id = hex(sha256('codepet-ev1|' + client + '|' + kind + '|' + session + '|' + dig + '|' + floor(at_ms / 3000)))[..32]
event_ids.session_field: the raw session id; for a Hermes approval event (no session_id) the literal '~ak:' + approval_key ('~' never occurs in an id, so it cannot collide)
notes: cases 1 and 2 share a 3 s bucket and dedupe; case 3 is the next bucket and does not
case 5 is a Hermes approval event (session field '~ak:<approval_key>')

interactivity.policy: positive headless evidence -> non-interactive; no evidence or /proc unreadable -> interactive

rules.claude-code: CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT starts with 'sdk' -> false; else if the variable is absent, the nearest ancestor (depth <= 4) whose comm is 'claude' has an argv token exactly '-p' or '--print' -> false; else true
rules.codex: nearest 'codex' ancestor (depth <= 4): argv[1] == 'e', or any argv token exactly 'exec' or 'review' -> false
rules.opencode: the plugin's process.argv has the exact token 'run' or 'serve' after the binary -> false (sent as payload 'interactive')
rules.grok-cli: session-mode field once WP7 confirms it; until then the nearest 'grok' ancestor (depth <= 4) has an exact token in headless_flags, a token starting with one of headless_prefixes, or the adjacent pair 'agent' 'headless' -> false. 'agent stdio' (IDE/ACP), 'agent serve' and 'agent leader' stay interactive
rules.hermes: the plugin decides: platform (remembered per session_id) in hermes_platforms -> sent (the hook and fold treat it as interactive); otherwise, or unknown -> not sent at all. Approval events carry no platform: they are sent only for surface 'cli' or 'transport:*' and are interactive. Consequence (notes.md): Hermes background or gateway work never reaches CodePet, so it can never set helpers_busy. Background-review agents per WP7

interactivity.grok_source: grok 1.0.52 (0920c8169e27) `grok --help` and `grok agent --help`, read 2026-10-16 under a throwaway HOME

turn_qualifies.rule: matching turn was open AND (tools >= 1 OR duration_ms >= min_turn_ms) AND interactive AND NOT test

caps.rule: jar_full if jar >= jar_max; else capped_session if any earned_at of this session > at - cap_session_ms; else capped_hour if count(earned_at > at - 1 h) >= cap_per_hour; else capped_day if count(earned_at > at - 24 h) >= cap_per_day; else allow. Windows are half-open: an earn exactly one window ago no longer counts. Forgotten rows (earned_at 0) never count.

defaults.now: each event folds with now = its at (no clamping in these vectors)

model.per_event_expect: state of the vector's session after the event, 'earned' = a treat dropped by this event
model.final_expect: treats = treats earned in the vector; finished_seq = meta.finished_seq increments; open_turn = open turn key or null

transitions.session_start: state idle (an ended session restarts idle)
transitions.turn_start: a still-open turn closes neutrally (no treat, no finished_seq); open the new turn (tools 0, started at); state working
transitions.activity: (a) a turn is open and (key == open turn, or the event has no turn key): waiting/idle -> working; a tool id not yet counted in that turn counts as a tool. An activity without a tool id (tool null: Hermes clarify/approval replies, OpenCode permission replies, a Claude activity without tool_use_id) never counts as a tool; it only changes the state. (b) key == last done turn, at <= last_done_ms + late_tool_ms and a tool id not counted in that turn: count it toward the finished turn; if that turn earned nothing and was not re-checked, re-run the treat check once (duration = last_done_ms - its start). A tool-less or already-counted late activity is (d) and never spends the re-check. (c) key == last done turn, at > last_done_ms + late_tool_ms and a tool id not counted in that turn: continuation - reopen the turn (same start, its tools + 1), state working. (d) otherwise only last_event_ms, except that a session in state waiting with no open turn returns to idle (the question was answered and nothing known is running)
transitions.waiting: state waiting (approval rows: their own row)
transitions.idle_prompt: state idle; the open turn stays open
transitions.turn_done: closes the open turn with the same key: state idle, finished_seq++ (interactive sessions only), treat check with tools = counted + payload tools. No matching open turn -> only last_event_ms
transitions.turn_failed: closes only the matching turn, no treat: state error, error_at_ms = at
transitions.turn_cancelled: closes only the matching turn, no treat: state idle. Keyless: closes the open turn only if it started before at
transitions.session_end: state ended; an open turn closes neutrally

model.approval_rows: Hermes approval_key events use a separate row keyed by HMAC(approval_key): waiting -> waiting; activity with the same key -> idle; nothing else touches it
model.non_interactive: tracked (state machine runs) but never counts for the face, never increments finished_seq and never earns
model.hello: the first non-test event of a client since Connect sets first_seen_ms and hello_seq++ (any interactivity); see fold_vectors

events.note: late tool of the finished turn
arrives in a later batch; at <= last_done + 1 s; re-check earns
a second prompt in the same turn

fold.rule: outcomes in order: duplicate (dedupe_key exists: unlink, no row change) -> dropped_off (meta.enabled = 0) -> dropped_old (at < now - max_event_age_ms) -> clamp (at > now + future_clamp_ms -> at = now, still folded) -> dropped_child -> test records: outcome test while meta.test_state == 'running', else dropped_test (a late or replayed ready-check record) -> client record (+hello) -> no_life (stop) -> folded
fold.test_records: the fold never changes meta.test_state/test_at_ms/test_client: it only keeps the agent_events row (test = 1, outcome test). The clients job owns the check: it sets test_state running (test_at_ms = now, test_client = the first tested client in client order) before writing the nonce and running the stored commands, then waits until every tested client has an agent_events row (client, test = 1, kind turn_done, outcome test, at_ms >= the job start) or test_done_delay_ms + test_arrival_ms passed, and sets done (all arrived) or failed (test_at_ms = now), removes $STATE/test.nonce and exports. Clients without a row get last_outcome failed, last_reason ready_check
fold.events_7d: COUNT(*) FROM agent_events WHERE client = ? AND test = 0 AND outcome IN ('folded','no_life') AND at_ms > now - agent_events_keep_ms. Dropped (off, old, child, test) and duplicate deliveries never count
fold.hook_nonce_cases: nonce matches / wrong / file missing are decided by the hook (normalization vectors with 'nonce'); only a matching record reaches the fold, and even then only while a check is running

aggregate.function: Rust agent::pet_state(session rows, meta.count_helpers, now) -> the export's agent.state, agent.apps, agent.stale_at_ms, agent.error_at_ms, agent.error_app and agent.helpers_busy (the seq/finished/hello/test fields come from meta). Pure; computed at every export from committed agent_sessions rows
aggregate.row_fields: client, approval (1 = Hermes approval-key row), interactive, state, state_since_ms, last_event_ms, error_at_ms
rules: a row counts for its app only when interactive = 1 and: state working and now < last_event_ms + stale_working_ms (expiry = that sum); state waiting and now < last_event_ms + stale_waiting_ms; state error and now < error_at_ms + error_recent_ms (expiry = error_at_ms + error_recent_ms). idle and ended rows never count. The edges are half-open: exactly stale_working_ms after the last event the row no longer counts
Hermes approval rows (approval = 1) are interactive and count like any row of client hermes (waiting only)

per app: the highest state over its counting rows (waiting > working > error); since_ms = the smallest state_since_ms among its counting rows in that state; stale_at_ms = the largest expiry among them (the app keeps that state until its last such row expires)
apps: one entry per app with a counting row, sorted by since_ms, then client order
state: the highest app state, idle when apps is empty

stale_at_ms: the smallest apps[].stale_at_ms, null when apps is empty. A lower state of another row of the same app reappears at the next export (that row's next event), not by a timer; this is the accepted bound of the no-polling rule
error_at_ms / error_app: the largest error_at_ms over interactive non-approval rows of any state with now < error_at_ms + error_recent_ms (ties: client order); else both null
helpers_busy: count_helpers and some row with interactive = 0, state working and now < last_event_ms + stale_working_ms. Non-interactive rows never reach apps, state, error_* or a face
the aggregate ignores meta.enabled; the shared priority shows Off first

hmac_keys.formula: key = lowercase hex(HMAC-SHA256(meta.hook_salt, domain + US + client + US + part1 [+ US + part2 ...]))[..32], US = the byte 0x1f. Parts are the raw ids from the inbox record (ids are [A-Za-z0-9._:-], so neither US nor '~' can occur in them)

approval.column: agent_sessions.session_key (approval = 1); its own domain, so it never collides with a session key

turn.column: open_turn_key, last_done_turn_key, activity_turns.turn_key, agent_events.turn_hmac. A turn_start without a turn key uses turn = '~ev:' + event_id

parts: session field of the event id

priority.function: shared_priority(export, now, seen) -> face. Generated into petstate.js as sharedPriority (WP6) and used by the bar cell, Home and the overlay. Not Rust agent::pet_state, which is the aggregate that builds export.agent (see 'aggregate')

order.when: life == null (first run, or after a goodbye/death; memorial.count does not matter)
life.armed == false (the owner's upgraded Ginger before Let's go!)
life.fainted, else life.paused (pet.pause; no UI sets it in v0.3), else care.sleeping
a need is empty (now) or critical
a counting app is working; else agent.test.state == 'running' and now < test.at_ms + test_done_delay_ms + test_arrival_ms (the ready check types about 1.5 s)
grew up (unseen_events), a new test done, hello or finished_seq inside its window

home_controls.fainted: only the two tiles that revive
home_controls.other: 4 tiles, 3 round buttons, Treats when treats_visible

priority.need_pick: among needs at the highest present group (now/critical first, then soon), pick by need_priority; the line uses that need's own level
priority.counting_app: an agent.apps entry whose stale_at_ms > now
priority.app_order: agent.apps order (since_ms ascending, then client order); {app} is the first app in the row's set, {app2} the second
priority.waiting_app: the waiting app with the latest since_ms (ties: client order)

celebrate.grew: unseen_events is not empty (stage journal entries not yet marked seen). No time window and no wake: it stays until Home has shown it, then the popup calls pet.events_seen {life_id, through_seq: the largest seq} (the bar and the overlay never call it). Bubble: star + confetti
celebrate.test: agent.test.state == 'done' and test.at_ms > seen.test_at_ms and now < at_ms + celebrate_window_ms
celebrate.hello: hello_seq > seen.hello_seq and now < hello_at_ms + celebrate_window_ms
celebrate.finished: finished_seq > seen.finished_seq and now >= finished_at_ms + celebrate_grace_ms and now < finished_at_ms + celebrate_window_ms and finished_app is not a counting working app

lines.finished: act.done_full if finished_jar_full, else act.done_treat if finished_treat, else act.done

celebrate.seen: the UI records the celebrated seq/at and passes it back as `seen`

priority.treats_visible: enabled and treats.jar > 0 and the life is awake (not care.sleeping), not paused and not fainted
priority.star_badge: rows 7-9 show the star badge when treats_visible
priority.wake_at_ms: null when Off, without a life and for welcome. Otherwise the minimum of these future times (null when none), whatever row wins: stale_at_ms of each counting app; the testing end (test.at_ms + test_done_delay_ms + test_arrival_ms) while running and ahead; for each unseen time-windowed celebration candidate whose window is still open, its grace end if still ahead, else its window end; the error frame end and the oops end while ahead
priority.vars: exactly the placeholders of the line template; {app}/{app2} are client ids (the UI maps them to display names)

popup_routing.function: route(export) -> the screen the popup shows when it opens or after any export while open
rules_in_order: enabled == false and life != null -> off_look (Home variant: dimmed sleeping pet, off.line, Turn on)
enabled == false and life == null -> first_run_off (the picker with the Turn on footer instead of Let's go!; Let's go! is never offered while Off)
life == null and memorial.count == 0 -> first_run (picker, cat preselected, Let's go!)
life == null and memorial.count > 0 -> memorial (memorial.line with memorial.latest_name, Meet a new pet -> first_run for this popup session only; UI-local, not stored)
life.armed == false -> welcome_back (picker preselecting the life's look, name kept, Let's go! = pet.start on that life)
transitions: a left click on the Off bar cell calls app.set_enabled {enabled:true} first, then routes (one click turns CodePet on and opens Home)

the power switch flipped to Off on any screen (Helpers, More, Help, Change, a row sheet) routes to off_look / first_run_off at once; flipped back On, the popup routes again (Home, not the sub-page it was on)
after a successful pet.start the UI calls clients.status and shows connect_card when connect_card.offered is not empty, else home; closing the popup on the card counts as Not now
after pet.retire (Say goodbye) the next route is memorial

connect_card.function: offered(clients.status result) -> the apps on the first-run Connect card, all pre-ticked
connect_card.rule: every client in client order except codex with installed and not connected and job == null (a client whose last Connect failed is offered again). Empty -> the card is skipped

helpers_rows.function: helper_row(client id, export client record or null, now, tz_offset_min) -> how its Helpers row and row sheet look
rules_in_order: no record, or installed == false and connected == false -> hidden (no row)
job running: kind connect -> row.connecting; disconnect -> row.disconnecting; test -> row.testing. spinner, no step, no Stop watching
failed_reason != null -> row.failed + reason.<reason_to_copy>, step btn.retry (clients.connect), Stop watching when connected
needs_step == codex_hooks_off -> row.codex.off, step btn.showme (the Codex guide's codex.off page), Stop watching when connected
needs_step == codex_trust -> row.step, step btn.showme (the Codex trust guide codex.step1..5), Stop watching when connected
connected and first_seen_ms == null -> row.waiting with hint.open shown at once on the list; the sheet adds hint.claude2 for claude-code. Stop watching
connected -> row.seen.<bucket> of last_seen_ms (first_seen_ms when last_seen_ms is null). Stop watching
not connected, codex -> row.codex.new, step btn.connect

seen_buckets.now: now - seen < seen_just_now_ms (including a seen time in the future)
seen_buckets.today: otherwise, the same local calendar day as now
seen_buckets.yesterday: the local calendar day before now's
seen_buckets.local_day: floor((ms + tz_offset_min * 60000) / 86400000); the UI uses Qt's local date, so DST is the system's

helpers_rows.connect_all: the ids of visible rows that are not connected, have no running job and are not codex (a failed row counts); the button is hidden when the list is empty
